subject: Micro-trial top-up: escrow, SLA waiver, and milestone credits
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@averysys.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Micro-trial top-up request — escrow & SLA question

Hey Jasmine,

Quick one — engineering ramped our usage during the pilot and we're about to hit our timebox cap next week. We'd like to extend the micro-trial by 3 weeks, but procurement is asking for two things before sign-off: 1) a short-term credit/escrow arrangement instead of an invoice for the extension, and 2) a temporary SLA waiver around latency for early-stage load tests.

Can Redwood issue a quote that shows: a) 3-week extension cost (billable as credits held in escrow until the pilot milestones are met), b) the milestone definitions (basic success criteria for release-ready integration), and c) a clear statement on the temporary SLA waiver scope?

Also need any redlineable language that legal can review quickly. If we can move fast, procurement can get PO out this week.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Avery Systems

[Attachment: internal-consumer-usage-snapshot.csv]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@averysys.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Micro-trial top-up request — escrow & SLA question

Samir — thanks for the context and the usage snapshot. I ran this past finance/legal and sketched two options below so procurement has choices. I attached a compact quote and a one-page amendment you can share with legal.

Option A — Credit Escrow (recommended for speed):
- 3-week extension = 75,000 tokens equivalent (estimated) billed as 100% credit held in escrow by Redwood until milestone verification.
- Escrow holdback: Redwood will allocate credits to Avery; unused credits refund back to Avery if milestones fail.
- Milestone verification: 2 integration smoke tests (API throughput at 50 p50 latency) + one production-ish end-to-end demo with your SREs.
- Temporary SLA waiver: Redwood will exclude latency SLO penalties for pre-production load test windows explicitly dated in the amendment. Reliability and data retention unaffected.

Option B — Prepaid Invoice with Conditional Refund:
- Same token quantity billed via invoice; 20% held as refundable retention for unmet milestones (refund via credit).
- Simpler bookkeeping for procurement; slightly longer finance lead time.

Next steps I propose: I can send the amendment with either A or B language redline-ready. If procurement prefers escrow, DocuSign flow + short PO to expedite kickoff. Attached: redwood-microtrial-quote.pdf and a draft micropilot-amendment-docusign.pdf.

If you want, David can add the payable/escrow mechanics for legal. LMK which option you prefer and I’ll fire the DocuSign.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-microtrial-quote.pdf]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Micro-trial top-up request — escrow & SLA question

Jasmine — thanks, looks good. A couple notes from legal/finance before we send to Avery:
- For Option A (escrow), we need explicit wording on the escrow agent/flow. If it's Redwood-managed credit hold, call it an "escrowed credit pool" and explain reconciliation cadence (we suggest 7 days after milestone verification).
- Define milestone failure refund timing (we recommend refund within 14 days as credit or invoice offset).
- SLA waiver: tighten scope to "pre-production load tests" and include explicit start/end timestamps and call out metric exceptions (latency p95/p99 excluded).
- Add a one-sentence privacy/data clause clarifying no change to data residency or logging.

I'll mark up the amendment (micropilot-amendment-docusign.pdf) with suggested language for escrow mechanics and refund timing. If procurement requests an independent third-party escrow, note that will add 5–7 business days.

David
David Kim
Director, Finance & Legal (Contracts), Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed amendment & DocuSign — micro-trial extension

Samir — attaching the updated amendment with David's language added and a clean DocuSign envelope ready. Summary of the final proposal:

- Option chosen: Credit Escrow (A) — Redwood-managed escrowed credit pool.
- Token allocation: 75,000 tokens for a 3-week extension (usage estimate from your snapshot).
- Escrow mechanics: Credits allocated to Avery's account immediately; reconciliation and milestone verification within 7 days of demo; refund (if any) issued as account credit within 14 days.
- SLA waiver: Limited to the pre-production load test windows noted in Section 2 of the amendment (dates to be filled in at signing). Production SLAs remain intact.
- Billing: No upfront invoice; DocuSign acts as authorization to allocate credits and start the extension.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PoA?envelopeId=abc123

If this matches procurement's appetite I'll send the envelope and CC procurement mailbox. If procurement wants third-party escrow, let us know — that will add time.

Thanks — Jasmine
